newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds rallied into the close on Wednesday with Bunds, after sagging through the afternoon, to end higher with the market still watching tap sales of the Dutch benchmark 10-year issue, dealers said.

Dutch bonds started brightly in the morning, prompting the finance ministry to raise the price on the 5.75 percent February 2007 tap to 99.75 from 99.55 overnight, but after an early spurt of business, interest began to wane, one broker said.
The price was cut back again to 99.50 shortly before the close and the tap was left open with 3.2 billion guilders raised so far.

Dealers were divided on how much the ministry would seek to raise through the tap, some had been expecting as little as 3.25 billion while others were looking for the tranche to remain open until five to 7.5 billion was raised.
"I heard that they don't want to raise too much this time as it would leave them with nothing to do for the rest of the year," one trader said.
On May 14, the Finance Ministry said only 10 billion guilders of its 1997 borrowing requirement remained and some in the market said there were rumours that this may even have been overstated.

The tap sales already concluded were encouraging, traders said, taking the 5.75 percent 2007 bond over the 10 billion guilder level usually regarded as the minimum for a liquid benchmark by foreign investors.
Initial sales in January raised 7.5 billion guilders.
Sales in the tap issue will continue from 0700 GMT to 1500 GMT until further notice.
